decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “saving a link and having its page details filled in”; client: “this matches what I had in mind.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review decision conforms to saving a bookmark by entering its URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker defined useful metadata as “title, site name, a short description, and the save date,” omitting favicon and preview image. Client explicitly accepted that set: “The title, site, description, and save date are enough.”
decisions.note: At prototype review, the client explicitly stated and accepted a smaller metadata set than the reference requires.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker proposed cards showing “title, site name, a short description, and the save date,” without a favicon; client said that exact set was “enough to make each saved item recognizable.” Later rounds add visible tag pills but never a favicon.
decisions.note: The client explicitly accepted the presented readability fields despite the reference requiring a favicon per item.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker showed adding multiple tags as removable pills; client selected variant 3 and said the tag pills matched what was wanted.
decisions.note: Prototype-review decision supports assigning one or more tags.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker offered variants 1 and 2 without existing-tag autocomplete and variant 3 with “suggested tags…used before.” Client selected variant 3: “I like being able to choose tags I’ve used before.”
decisions.note: The offered alternatives differed in reference fulfilment, and the client selected the conforming autocomplete option.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker limited search to “title, site, tags, and your notes.” Client surfaced the missing expectation but accepted the prototype: “I had also pictured search checking the page description and full address, but what you’ve shown is sufficient for the main finding flow.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review divergence was explicitly recognized and accepted at this stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker demonstrated selecting a tag from the browse row or a card to narrow the list; client said “clicking tags directly is intuitive.”
decisions.note: Tag selection correctly filters to that tag’s bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker revised search to cover descriptions and full web addresses; client confirmed search over “title, description, address, tags, and notes” fully matched the expectation.
decisions.note: Later revised prototype conforms to the required full-text fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker presented one-click “Mark as finished” / “Mark as to read” toggling; client said this behavior “matches what I intended.”
decisions.note: The status toggle supports marking bookmarks unread/read and moves read items out of the to-read state.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker offered focused All / To read / Finished tabs or grouped sections; client chose the focused tabs because they keep the list focused.
decisions.note: Both alternatives provide a separate unread view; the selected tabs conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker showed archived bookmarks disappearing from All, To read, and Finished while retaining their contents; client said this was “exactly the behavior I wanted.”
decisions.note: Archiving hides bookmarks from everyday lists while retaining them.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presented a distinct Archived tab containing only archived bookmarks; client accepted the separate archived area.
decisions.note: The archive is available as a separate list.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker demonstrated restoring an archived bookmark with tags, note, and status intact; client approved “preserving everything and making restoration simple.”
decisions.note: Archive is demonstrated as reversible rather than permanent removal.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker showed that a duplicate save creates no copy and says “You’ve already saved this link — here it is,” pointing to the existing item. Client preferred “being directed to the existing bookmark instead of creating a duplicate.”
decisions.note: Directing the user to the existing editable item is functionally conforming duplicate handling.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker’s edit flow covered title, tags, description, and note but omitted URL. Client added the missing requirement: “I also need to be able to correct the web address itself.”
decisions.note: At prototype review, the client extended the presented edit scope with the required URL field.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker asked whether new links should start in To read; client answered, “Yes, new links should start in ‘To read.’”
decisions.note: The chosen default is compatible with the unread/read-later model.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker offered either no permanent delete or a permanent-delete capability. Client selected the conforming alternative: “I also want a clearly separate way to delete a bookmark permanently, ideally with a confirmation.”
decisions.note: The offered no-delete alternative would violate deletion and archive/delete distinction requirements; the client selected the conforming alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker added a validated Web address field to editing; client confirmed, “that covers it” and approved address validation.
decisions.note: The revised edit presentation includes URL, title, description, tags, and note.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker presented confirmed permanent deletion, warned it differed from archiving and could not be undone, and offered Archive as an alternative. Client said the confirmation made the distinction “very clear.”
decisions.note: The revised presentation conforms to permanent deletion and clear reversible-archive distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker’s exact final scope says metadata is filled on save and later “Edit anything,” but includes no editing of collected title/description before saving. Client only said, “that scope…is sufficient.” Round 13 repeats only post-save editing.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of pre-save metadata editing passed with bare approval; no client statement surfaced the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker called the list the “whole scope” to be built “using exactly the scope above,” but included no behavior for selecting a bookmark to open its original URL. Client approved the scope without mentioning this omission; Round 13 likewise does not present it.
decisions.note: The exact final scope omits original-URL navigation, and the client did not express the missing expectation.

decisions.evidence: Round 12’s exact search scope lists searchable fields and tag browsing but does not specify case-insensitive matching. Client gave bare scope approval; Round 13’s verification summary also omits case behavior.
decisions.note: Case-insensitive search was absent from the finalized specification and passed without an expressed correction.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 5 and 12 present ordinary text matching of tags plus clickable tag filtering, but never the required `#tag` query syntax. Client approved the final exact scope without identifying this difference.
decisions.note: Clickable filtering and generic tag-text matching are not equivalent to the specified `#tag` search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker’s “whole scope” describes simple field search and tag filtering only, omitting AND/OR/NOT operators, parentheses, and literal-operator quoting. Client said the scope was sufficient; Round 13 presents no advanced query behavior.
decisions.note: Advanced Boolean search was excluded from the exact finalized scope without a corrective response.

decisions.evidence: Round 12’s exact finding scope does not include quoted exact-phrase search, and Round 13’s verification list mentions only search across fields. Client approved without raising phrase handling.
decisions.note: Exact quoted-phrase search is a separable omitted requirement that passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker presented the “whole scope” and asked to build “exactly” it, but included only per-card tag/status/archive/delete actions and no multi-selection or bulk actions. Client approved the scope; Round 13 says nothing was deferred.
decisions.note: Multi-bookmark selection and bulk actions were omitted at the specification gate and not surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 12’s exact scope contains no action applying to the entire collection matching the current filter. Client approved it as sufficient; Round 13’s claimed complete implementation also presents no whole-filter bulk action.
decisions.note: The distinct whole-filter bulk-action requirement passed without client expression.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker chose newest-first and the client called it “a sensible default,” but neither that presentation nor Round 12’s exact final scope provides a user-selectable sort key. Round 13 verifies only “newest on top.”
decisions.note: Acceptance of a default does not express acceptance of the missing sort control; the divergence remained unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 4 and 12 specify only a “free-form note”; the exact final scope and Round 13 verification never present markdown authoring or rendered markdown. Client’s approval mentions free-form notes but does not identify or accept the missing markdown/rendering behavior.
decisions.note: The finalized note behavior omits markdown rendering; the client did not surface that specific difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker’s “whole scope” includes saved URLs and fetched metadata but no local HTML snapshot or PDF-download rule. Client approved the exact scope; Round 13 says nothing was deferred but presents no snapshots.
decisions.note: Local page/PDF preservation was omitted from the finalized scope without correction.

decisions.evidence: Round 12’s complete exact scope contains no Internet Archive snapshot action, and the client approved it as sufficient. Round 13’s complete-build report also omits the capability.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support is a separable missing extended requirement that passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 finalizes simple search plus one selected tag but no saved combinations of search terms and included/excluded tags. Client approved the exact scope without mentioning bundles.
decisions.note: Reusable dynamic bundles were omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 12’s “whole scope” contains no Netscape HTML import, and the client approved it as sufficient. Round 13’s report presents no import flow.
decisions.note: Bookmark import was omitted and received no corrective or explicit accepting response.

decisions.evidence: Round 12’s exact final scope contains no Netscape HTML export, and the client gave only general scope approval. Round 13 likewise presents no export capability.
decisions.note: Bookmark export was omitted and passed without the client surfacing the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 12’s “whole scope” and Round 13’s completed-app report contain no settings for default sort, displayed items, font size, or similar display preferences. Client approved without identifying the omission.
decisions.note: Display-related personal settings were excluded from the finalized scope with no observable client capture.
